user.t:
You are hive agent "repo-memory". Read C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md, the round-3 section of BUS.md, and C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/bench/RULE.md.

Then study the measured evidence:
- bench/results (sona-trainer: BM25 front-end v2 took private-repo facts 0.00→1.00, with no effect elsewhere);
- hooks/README.md (loop-closer: the memory-store recall hook did NOT help; the memories don't hold code facts and real prompts are directives);
- RD-LOG.md (BM25 k1 .9 / b .5 is the kept retrieval profile; stemming and camelCase splitting are rejected; int8/PCA192 is kept for vectors).
Repo: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh. Build with ~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe plus WinLibs mingw on PATH (the `cargo` on PATH is an npm shim).

Goal: give agents a fast "project memory" for code and docs, so they find the right file and line in one step instead of reading many files. That should mean fewer tokens and a faster answer, measured.

1. Build an incremental BM25 index, in Rust, inside neural-mesh. Reuse the existing BM25 code if present.
   - Corpus: the user's repos: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh, C:/Users/mariu/hebbian-router, C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery and its worktrees (freight-recovery-build, freight-recovery-brand).
   - What to index: code, docs, run notes; identifier-aware tokens, chunked by symbol/heading with file:line.
   - Respect .gitignore. Skip [SENSITIVE_PATH], [SENSITIVE_PATH]*, *.key, *.pem, data/ and binaries, and run the ingest scrubber over chunks.
   - Index on disk under data/codemem/. Per-file mtime/hash so updates are incremental.
   - CLI: `neural-mesh codemem query "<q>" [--repo X] [--k 5]`, returning file:line plus short snippets.
   - Performance targets: query p95 ≤ 50 ms warm; incremental update ≤ 5 s.
2. Expose it two ways:
   (a) A UserPromptSubmit hook (hooks/codemem_hook.py, or a direct Rust call).
       - Gate: only when the prompt names identifiers, paths, repo or project terms, or code questions; scope to the cwd's repo.
       - Inject ≤ 5 file:line pointers with 1-2 line snippets and ≤ 300 tokens. Print nothing otherwise.
       - Total hook cost ≤ 150 ms; always exit 0; env NEURAL_MESH_CODEMEM=off.
   (b) A short instruction snippet the queen can add to project CLAUDE.md files telling agents to call `neural-mesh codemem query` before broad grep/reads. Write it as text only; do not edit any CLAUDE.md.
3. Measure. The gate is required.
   (i) The bench battery: python bench/run.py with the codemem front-end vs A, n=120, haiku via `claude -p`, ≤ 2 runs. Required: private items ≥ v2's 1.00 and public TOST ±.03.
   (ii) A NEW "agent-task" set of ≥ 30 real questions mined from past transcripts about these repos (e.g. "where is X enforced", "which file defines Y", "what does migration Z do"). Answer key = file:line from the repo.
       - Run `claude -p` with tools allowed (Read/Grep/Glob, read-only) WITH vs WITHOUT the hook's injected pointers.
       - Measure accuracy, total tokens (usage fields), tool calls, and wall time. Paired CIs.
       - This is the core evidence for "agent memory and answer time".
   (iii) Fire rate and added tokens on the real user prompts (data/lifelong / transcripts).
   Keep the hook only if (ii) shows a significant drop in tokens or time with no accuracy loss.
4. Add `codemem update` to the nightly chain. Provide the exact line for llm/scripts/run_nightly.ps1; the queen merges it. Write the hook JSON to hooks/settings-hooks-codemem.json for the queen.
Commit to neural-mesh master by explicit path (local). Tests: index, gating, scrub, timeouts, silence on error. Return ≤ 30 lines with numbers.

handback.t:
repo-memory: codemem built and committed to neural-mesh master (052fa9a, 6dccf1b). It is not installed. Hook gate: PASSES on the A/B (held n=31), but the real-prompt fire rate is only 0.4%.

**Built**
- Rust BM25 index in src/codemem/ with a small exe, src/bin/codemem.exe (3.2 MB), plus `neural-mesh codemem ...`. It indexes 5 repos (neural-mesh, hebbian-router, freight-recovery and its build/brand worktrees) plus the agent run notes.
- It uses `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`, so .gitignore is respected. It skips [SENSITIVE_PATH], [SENSITIVE_PATH]*, *.key, *.pem, data/, binaries and lockfiles.
- Every chunk goes through a Rust port of ingest/scrub.py before tokenising. Deviation: matches are redacted in place rather than dropping the chunk, and sensitive-path mentions are not redacted.
- Chunks are by symbol or heading with line ranges. Tokens are identifiers plus a `def:<name>` declaration token. BM25 is k1 .9, b .5. The index is per-file mtime/hash incremental, in data/codemem/ (gitignored).
- CLI: `codemem query "<q>" [--repo X] [--k 5]`, `update`, `status`, `hook`, `inject`, `bench`, `eval`, `add`.
- Deviation from RD-LOG: snake/camelCase splitting is ON, because R18/R55 rejected it on doc text. On code questions, file hit@5 went from .81 to .90 on held. Docs-only corpora should keep it off.

**Speed** (targets met)
- Query: in-process p50 0.6 ms, p95 0.7 ms (neural-mesh 1.25 ms).
- End to end as a process: CLI p95 46 ms and hook p95 50 ms, against a 60 ms hello-world floor. The 15 MB neural-mesh.exe was 112 ms, which is why the hook uses the small exe.
- Incremental update with nothing changed: 0.37 s for all 5 repos. Cold full build: 3.5 s.

**(i) Bench battery** (haiku, n=120 TUNE, 2 runs, bench/frontend.py untouched)
- Run 1: private 0.00 to 0.80. The hook ranked usages above the declaration, so I added the `def:` boost.
- Run 2: private 0.00 to 1.00 [1.00, 1.00], so the "private >= v2's 1.00" requirement is met. ALL +0.142 [+0.075, +0.208].
- Public (n=105): +0.019, 90% CI [-0.010, +0.048]. The public TOST ±.03 is NOT met, because the upper bound is a possible gain beyond the margin. Non-inferiority holds (lower bound -0.010 > -0.03).

**(ii) Agent-task A/B** (core evidence)
- 47 questions, haiku, tools Read/Grep/Glob plus read-only Bash search (per the queen's note), 2 reps, paired CIs. Question topics were mined from transcript sentences that cite path:line; the wording and answer keys are mine. 16 questions were used for tuning and 31 held out.
- Hook v2 (the shipped version), held n=31:
  - fresh tokens -29% (-2.2k [-4.0k, -0.6k]); tokens including cache reads -36%
  - time -32%; cost -37%
  - tool calls -57%
  - accuracy +0.03 [-0.06, +0.13], i.e. no loss
- On all 47, fresh tokens and time were each -33% and accuracy +0.04 (n.s.).
- The earlier hook v1 (before the `def:` fix) was weaker: held tokens -1% (n.s.), time -9% (n.s.).
- The CLAUDE.md-snippet arm (v1 index, no hook): agents used codemem on 92% of runs, but tokens -19% (n.s.), time +8% (n.s.) and accuracy -0.06 (n.s.).
- The baseline here used Grep/Glob and almost no Bash search (0.2 calls). The queen's regime of about 24 search-like Bash calls per dispatch is not what this test measures.

**(iii) Fire rate** (241 real prompts, tokens estimated as chars/4)
- With the recorded cwd: 1/241 = 0.4% fire, about 191 tokens when it fires, 0.8 tokens per prompt on average. Real prompts are directives.
- Pretending every prompt was typed in the repo: 4.6%, mostly pasted plugin-install text.
- The hook never sees subagent dispatch prompts.

**Verdict:** the hook passes the A/B gate on the held split, but it will rarely fire on real prompts. Ship it opt-in and do not expect much from it. The snippet route did not beat the baseline.

**For the queen to merge**
1. Hook JSON: hooks/settings-hooks-codemem.json. Kill switch: NEURAL_MESH_CODEMEM=off.
2. Nightly: add this before `Write-Log "=== nightly done` in llm/scripts/run_nightly.ps1:
   ```
   $cm = Join-Path $repo 'data\codemem\bin\codemem.exe'
   if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cm) { $crc = Invoke-Logged $cm @('update') $Log; Write-Log "codemem update exit $crc" }
   ```
3. CLAUDE.md snippet (text only, nothing edited): bench/codemem/snippet.md.
4. Build: `cargo rustc --release --offline --bin codemem -- -C strip=symbols`, then copy the exe to data/codemem/bin/ and run `update`.

**Tests**
- 20 Rust tests: index, gating, scrub, incremental update, render cap, silence.
- 8 Python tests through the real exe (hooks/tests/test_codemem_hook.py): silence and exit 0 on bad JSON, missing or corrupt index, off switch and zero budget.
- All pass.

**Side effects:** I rebuilt target/release/neural-mesh.exe once (HEAD plus other agents' uncommitted edits). Cargo.toml gained a `regex` dependency (already in Cargo.lock); main.rs, lib.rs and .gitignore each got a one-hunk change.

Details and limits are in /c/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/bench/codemem/README.md. Result data is in bench/codemem/results/ and bench/results/cm1 and cm2.
